blocks.text: Essential Excel for office managers on Mac shortcuts

Keyboard shortcuts are the fastest way to handle Excel on Mac. Stop reaching for your mouse for every action. Use ⌘ + T to turn a range of data into a table instantly. This adds filters and formatting automatically. Use ⌃ + Space to select an entire column. Use ⇧ + Space to select an entire row. These simple movements keep your hands on the keyboard.
Managing data in Excel for office managers

Office managers often handle messy data from multiple sources. You might export lists from Slack or project management tools. Always check your data types. Excel sometimes treats numbers as text, which breaks calculations. If your SUM formula returns zero, check if your numbers are aligned to the left. That usually means they are formatted as text. You can fix this by using the Text to Columns feature in the Data tab.

Pivot tables are your best friend for summarizing office expenses or attendance logs. Select your data range and go to Insert > PivotTable. Drag your fields into the Rows or Values areas to see totals immediately. This avoids manual counting or complex formulas that are prone to mistakes. Once you have a pivot table, you can refresh it whenever you add new data to your source table.

blocks.text: Always use cell references. If you type =500+200, you have to edit the formula later. If you type =A1+B1, you just change the numbers in the cells. Your formulas update automatically. This is a basic rule of spreadsheet hygiene. It saves you from redoing work when numbers change.

faq.question: Can I use Excel on Mac if I am used to Windows?
faq.answer: Yes. Most features are the same, but some keyboard shortcuts differ. You can customize your shortcuts in System Settings if needed.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my Excel files?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It points, explains, and guides you so you can perform the work yourself.

faq.question: What is the best way to learn Excel for office managers?
faq.answer: Start by mastering tables, pivot tables, and basic functions like SUM, COUNTIF, and XLOOKUP. Practice with real data from your daily tasks.
